`grep`: print lines that match a pattern.

## Synopsis

<strong>grep</strong> \[<strong>-ivnclqhHFE</strong>\] <em>pattern</em> \[<em>file</em>...\]\
<strong>grep</strong> \[<strong>-ivnclqhHFE</strong>\]\
<strong>-e</strong> <em>pattern</em> \[<strong>-e</strong> <em>pattern</em>\]... \[<em>file</em>...\]

## Description

<strong>grep</strong> reads each <em>file</em> and prints the lines that match any <em>pattern</em>. With no <em>file</em>, or where a <em>file</em> is <strong>-</strong>, it reads standard input. With more than one file, each line printed starts with its file's name and a colon.

A <em>pattern</em> is a POSIX basic regular expression (BRE), or with <strong>-E</strong> an extended one (ERE), as far as Lua's patterns can express them:

<strong>.</strong>
: any character

<strong>\*</strong>
: the item before it, any number of times

<strong>^</strong> and <strong>$</strong>
: the start of the line (first in the pattern) and its end (last)

<strong>\[...\]</strong> and <strong>\[^...\]</strong>
: a set of characters, or any character not in it; ranges such as <strong>a-z</strong> and the classes <strong>\[:alpha:\]</strong>, <strong>\[:digit:\]</strong>, <strong>\[:alnum:\]</strong>, <strong>\[:space:\]</strong>, <strong>\[:upper:\]</strong>, <strong>\[:lower:\]</strong>, <strong>\[:punct:\]</strong>, <strong>\[:xdigit:\]</strong> and <strong>\[:cntrl:\]</strong> work inside it (with <strong>-i</strong>, <strong>\[:upper:\]</strong> and <strong>\[:lower:\]</strong> are any letter)

<strong>\\</strong><em>c</em>
: the character <em>c</em> itself

<strong>+</strong> and <strong>?</strong>
: with <strong>-E</strong> only: one or more, zero or one of the item before; in a BRE they are plain characters

Groups, alternation and intervals (<strong>\\( \\)</strong>, <strong>\\\|</strong>, <strong>\\\{n,m\\\}</strong>, or with <strong>-E</strong> <strong>( ) \| \{ \}</strong>) are not supported: such a pattern is refused with a message.

## Options

<strong>-e</strong> <em>pattern</em>
: Use <em>pattern</em> as a pattern; may be given more than once. Every argument that is not an option is then a <em>file</em>.

<strong>-E</strong>
: Patterns are extended regular expressions.

<strong>-F</strong>
: Patterns are fixed strings, matched as they are.

<strong>-i</strong>
: Ignore case.

<strong>-v</strong>
: Select the lines that do not match.

<strong>-n</strong>
: Put each line's number (and a colon) before it.

<strong>-c</strong>
: Print only a count of the selected lines, for each file.

<strong>-l</strong>
: Print only the names of the files with a selected line (<strong>(standard input)</strong> for standard input).

<strong>-q</strong>
: Print nothing; exit 0 at the first selected line.

<strong>-h</strong>
: Never put file names before lines.

<strong>-H</strong>
: Always put file names before lines.

<strong>--</strong>
: The arguments after it are all files.

Single-letter options may be combined, as in <strong>-in</strong>.

## Exit status

0 if a line was selected, 1 if none was, 2 for an error (a bad option or pattern, or a file that could not be opened), unless <strong>-q</strong> found a line.

## Examples

```text
grep -n require /bin/ls
grep -ic "^local" *.lua
ps | grep -v sh
grep -E "ab+c?" notes.txt
```

## Notes

There are no context options (<strong>-A</strong>, <strong>-B</strong>, <strong>-C</strong>), no <strong>-r</strong> and no <strong>-o</strong>.

## See also

<strong>find</strong>(1), <strong>head</strong>(1), <strong>tail</strong>(1), <strong>sh</strong>(1)
